`UnifiedActivationPipeline` (`.aios-core/development/scripts/unified-activation-pipeline.js`) is the single entry point for all 12 agents; `generate-greeting.js` delegates to `UnifiedActivationPipeline.activate(agentId)`. `GreetingBuilder` assembles greetings with enriched context. `buildGreeting()` loads `loadUserProfile()` and passes it to `_buildContextualGreeting()` to avoid duplicate `resolveConfig()` calls. `GreetingPreferenceManager.getPreference(userProfile)` accepts optional `userProfile` for bob-mode restriction; PM bypasses it. Non-PM bob agents: `auto` redirects, forced `named` greets, commands empty. Pipeline: Phase 1, 5 parallel loaders (`Promise.all`); Phase 2, agent def; Phase 3, sequential preference/session type/workflow; Phase 4, enriched context; Phase 5, `GreetingBuilder`.

8 agents have `visibility: [full, quick, key]`; `qa`, `data-engineer`, `devops`, `ux-design-expert` lack it and fall back to first 12 commands. `aios-master` uses `visibility: full`. `*yolo` is universal. Badge: `_safeGetPermissionBadge()` in `greeting-builder.js`.

Mock `resolveConfig` with `mockReturnValue` (not `mockReturnValueOnce`) when called multiple times. `validate-user-profile.js` `validateUserProfile()` is pure (no filesystem). Always mock fs, js-yaml, config-resolver, and dependency modules BEFORE requiring the module under test. `resolveConfig()` merges L1-L5; L5 (`user-config.yaml`) has highest priority. `user_profile` is `USER_FIELD` in `migrate-config.js`; `toggleUserProfile()` in `config-resolver.js` flips bob<->advanced.

`PermissionMode` and `OperationGuard` in `.aios-core/core/permissions/` are functional. `index.js` wires `cycleMode()` and `enforcePermission()`. Mode cycle: `explore`(0) -> `ask`(1) -> `auto`(2) -- `PermissionMode.MODE_CYCLE`.

Formats: structured (`name: xxx`) and compact (`key: 'value'`); compact agents: qa, devops, data-engineer, ux-d
